title: Day 82 · Week 11, Day 5 — Protocol: the pelvic floor, week one — forty-six trials, the one woman in three who leaks after birth, the half who squeeze the wrong way, and the first seven days
summary: The pelvic floor training block begins. What the pelvic floor is (the levator ani sling that holds the bladder and bowel closed and the organs up) and what pregnancy and birth ask of it — in an MRI-based model the medial pubococcygeus stretches to 3.26 times its resting length. How common leaking is: 41% of pregnant women (44 studies, 88,305 women) and 31% in the year after birth, with prevalence at one year back near third-trimester levels. The 2020 Cochrane review (46 trials, 10,832 women): early, structured training in continent women cut incontinence in late pregnancy by 62% and at 3–6 months postpartum by 29% (high-quality evidence), with smaller effects in population programmes, no proven benefit for women already leaking, and almost no harms. The Trondheim trial (301 first-time mothers): 32% vs 48% leaking at 36 weeks, 20% vs 32% at three months — one in six prevented. Bump 1991: after verbal instruction only 49% contract correctly and 25% bear down. NICE NG210 and NG123: encourage for all, supervise for higher risk or existing leaks, at least 8 contractions three times a day, keep it up for life. How to find the muscles, the week-one plan, the knack, the warning signs and the father's part.
action: Tonight, set three daily reminders on her phone (and yours if you join in) tied to breakfast, lunch and brushing teeth, labelled 'squeeze, lift, let go'. Add a 'Pelvic floor' section to the pregnancy file with two lines: any leaking now, or a mother or sister with incontinence or prolapse (yes/no); and the question for the next visit — a referral to a pelvic health physiotherapist to check technique. First set tonight: five slow squeezes, lying down.
